item.message: Skill descriptions were shortened to fit the 2% skills context budget. Codex can still see every skill, but some descriptions are shorter. Disable unused skills or plugins to leave more room for the rest.

item.text: {"brief_complete":false,"completion_reason":"Three material architecture decisions remain around API compatibility, secret binding, and reproducible model identity.","questions":[{"decision_key":"public_api_version_compatibility","label":"API evolution","context":"`packages/central-client/index.mjs` is the shared command boundary for tests, Electron, HTTP, and WebSocket clients, while `services/nexus-node/src/run-coordinator.mjs` currently accepts `runs.submit`, `inference.submit،" ,"evidence":"`packages/central-client/index.mjs` gives every client one outcome-level command surface, and `services/nexus-node/src/run-coordinator.mjs` already maps several submission commands into the same run coordinator; the release plan has not decided how those clients survive future contract changes.","impact":"Existing local tools must keep working when NexusCentral changes its commands or response shapes.","question":"How should existing clients survive API changes?","choices":[{"number":1,"text":"Version contracts and retire aliases gradually","consequence":"Each request names an API version, and older aliases keep working through a documented deprecation window; this adds compatibility tests but permits controlled evolution."},{"number":2,"text":"Support only the latest contract","consequence":"Clients must update with NexusCentral immediately, which keeps the server simpler but makes independent integrations brittle."},{"number":3,"text":"Preserve every public alias indefinitely","consequence":"Old clients remain compatible without deadlines, but translation paths and maintenance costs accumulate permanently."}],"allow_multiple":false,"recommended_choice":1,"recommendation_reason":"It fits the existing shared client boundary and normalized coordinator without freezing early command shapes forever.","priority":91},{"decision_key":"workflow_secret_binding","label":"Secret binding","context":"Workflow definitions need credentials and environment settings, but provider profiles are intentionally secret-free and the host owns secure credential storage.","evidence":"`kits/providers-kit/index.mjs` stores secret-free provider profiles, while the verified host boundary keeps credentials in secure storage; workflow schedules and frozen versions therefore need a defined way to reference secrets without copying them into workflow records.","impact":"Scheduled work must remain reproducible without exposing one operator's credentials to collaborators or saved workflow data.","question":"How should workflows receive credentials and environment settings?","choices":[{"number":1,"text":"Use named host-managed bindings","consequence":"A frozen workflow stores a binding name, and the host resolves its current authorized secret when a run starts while recording only the binding version; rotation stays safe, though missing or unauthorized bindings stop the run."},{"number":2,"text":"Snapshot encrypted values per workflow version","consequence":"Every frozen version retains exactly what it needs, improving historical repeatability but multiplying sensitive copies and complicating rotation and revocation."},{"number":3,"text":"Use the starting operator's session","consequence":"Runs inherit the credentials of whoever starts them, which is simple for interactive work but makes schedules and shared workflows dependent on a particular user session."}],"allow_multiple":false,"recommended_choice":1,"recommendation_reason":"It preserves the recorded host-owned secret boundary while allowing frozen workflows and schedules to outlive individual sessions.","priority":94},{"decision_key":"resolved_model_identity","label":"Model identity","context":"Routes may choose among direct, LAN, and PeerJS providers, so a friendly model name can resolve to different artifacts or runtime configurations.","evidence":"`packages/contracts/index.mjs` spans several provider protocol families, and `kits/routing-kit/index.mjs` owns candidate selection and fallback; without a resolved identity, two runs using the same displayed model name may not be reproducible or comparable.","impact":"A completed run must reveal exactly which model and runtime produced its result, even after fallback or model updates.","question":"What should identify the model used by a run?","choices":[{"number":1,"text":"Record an immutable resolved identity","consequence":"Dispatch may use a friendly alias, but the run records provider, model revision or artifact hash, runtime, and settings profile; evidence stays reproducible at the cost of maintaining normalized identity records."},{"number":2,"text":"Record the provider's model string","consequence":"Runs store the name returned by the provider, which is easy to integrate but may silently refer to changing hosted revisions or local files."},{"number":3,"text":"Record only the selected alias","consequence":"The UI and workflows stay simple, but later audits cannot reliably distinguish fallback targets, upgraded artifacts, or runtime differences."}],"allow_multiple":false,"recommended_choice":1,"recommendation_reason":"It matches immutable run evidence and transport-neutral routing while still letting operators work with readable aliases.","priority":89}]}
